races.name: Industry Leading In-Play Markets At Unibet Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Big Bear Hug
runners_data.note: A hold-up specialist with 50 days off the track; Jim Boyle's runner has poor recent form (three finishes outside the top five) and has won just twice in 15 starts on similar going, suggesting fitness and AW form are both open questions here.
runners_data.comment: Big Bear Hug is yet to win but bounced back with a much-improved third last time out over today's distance and going, fitting with our rating of 79, the highest in this field. She carries a testing 140lb from stall three, with fifty days off the main query.

runners_data.name: Valentine Boy
runners_data.note: Won over 8f at Kempton on Standard in recent form and showed a creditable third over that trip; stepping up sharply to 1m3f is the key query, but Jude Fernandes has shown ability to wait and deliver, and the headgear change to a hood could sharpen his focus.
runners_data.comment: Valentine Boy won three starts back but has tailed off since, no better than eighth last time 18 days ago; our rating of 71 still shows him capable of better, fitted with a first-time hood and drawn five. That recent dip is the obvious worry.

runners_data.name: Sarangpur
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's four-year-old arrives in excellent recent form with back-to-back wins over 12f at Goodwood; true style is hold-up, and while this compressed tactical scenario is not ideal for a horse who benefits from a genuine gallop, the trip and course surface suit and T14 form (2/34) adds trainer context.
runners_data.comment: Sarangpur is in red-hot form, winning his last two starts over today's distance and backing up quickly just seven days ago; our rating of 68 nonetheless leaves him someway behind the pace-setters on figures. He is drawn seven today, with that modest overall level the main query.

runners_data.name: Sonnerie Power
runners_data.note: The T14 stat of 7/12 from David Killahena and Graeme McPherson is eye-catching; this seven-year-old carries all-weather experience (15/15 runs on similar going) and while its natural inclination is to come from off the pace, being pushed forward into a more prominent role by race circumstance is possible and may not be entirely against it.
runners_data.comment: Sonnerie Power has come right back into form, following a moderate middle spell with a smart second last time out over today's distance and going; our rating of 73 makes him second-best in this on that upward trend. A four-week absence is the only slight concern.

runners_data.name: Distinction
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old wearing a visor who has rarely threatened on Goodwood or Kempton Standard in recent starts; this horse's true racing style is hold-up but with modest recent figures (056836) and a poor record in similar going (1W1P from 15), it faces a stiff ask even in a weak field.
runners_data.comment: Distinction is yet to win but was third two starts back among mostly midfield efforts over today's distance and going; our rating of 66 places him mid-pack, fitted with a first-time visor. A modest sixth last time, 36 days ago, keeps expectations in check.

runners_data.name: Brodie's Boy
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's runner has a consistent profile of mid-division finishes in similar company and distance, with four placings from 11 starts on comparable going; though placed to be nearer the pace by the shape of this race, its natural inclination will still be to sit and wait, and it lacks the late acceleration spike to win a sprint finish decisively.
runners_data.comment: Brodie's Boy is yet to win, with a best of third four starts back among modest efforts over today's distance and going; our rating of 66 leaves him down the field at sixth of seven. A quick 15-day turnaround is the one thing in his favour.

runners_data.name: Maywedance
runners_data.note: Won over this exact 12f trip at Kempton on Standard going recently, which is the single most relevant piece of form in the race; John O'Shea's four-year-old (headgear: p) has a positive record on similar going (2W2P from 11) and James Glennon's experience as a 5lb claimer is the main risk in a contest that could get messy late.
runners_data.comment: Maywedance won two starts back and rounded off with a promising third last time out over today's distance and going, but our rating of 58 leaves her bottom of this field on figures. First-time cheekpieces are the sole change of note.

races.paceDynamic: This is an unusual race in that every single runner in the field is a hold-up type, meaning there is no natural front-runner or prominent racer to set a genuine pace over this 1m3f Kempton AW trip on Standard to Slow going. The race is almost certain to begin at a crawl, with horses jostling reluctantly for position before the tempo quickens sharply in the straight, producing a sprint finish from the home bend rather than a true test of stamina. In this tactical vacuum, the decisive factor will be who can quicken most sharply from a compressed, slow-run contest — horses with a turn of foot and strong recent form at the trip will hold a natural edge over those who need a truly run race to show their best. The field holds more genuine hold-up horses than can realistically sit last, so Sonnerie Power, Sarangpur, Distinction, and Brodie's Boy are the most likely to drift closer to midfield than they would prefer, with Valentine Boy and Big Bear Hug potentially the most experienced at navigating these tactical conditions. This race shape strongly favours horses with a sharp late burst and a positive recent record at this course and distance, since the slow pace will compress the field and place a premium on raw acceleration over the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint finish, late pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls for the first mile and the race ignites into a flat-out sprint over the final 2f.
scenarios.body: With no pace to run at, every runner will be queued up turning in, making the final two furlongs a pure speed test; a horse with a recent winning burst and good course form over this trip will have the clearest advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Compressed field, positional win
scenarios.trigger: If one or two runners are pushed forward against their nature to fill the pace vacuum and set a modest but steady gallop.
scenarios.body: A horse who secures an uncontested mid-group position with cover can dictate a controlled tempo and kick clear before rivals fully organise; Sonnerie Power or Brodie's Boy, nudged closer by circumstance, could benefit from accidentally finding daylight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers find traffic, race unresolved
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so slow that the field bunches badly in the straight and closers suffer severe interference.
scenarios.body: The compressed nature of a truly muddling gallop creates a lottery in the home straight, with horses checking and weaving; those drawn or ridden to track the widest path will avoid the worst of the trouble.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Strong traveller quickens clear
scenarios.trigger: If the going plays slower than expected and one horse travels conspicuously well through the race before producing an early decisive move.
scenarios.body: Standard to Slow conditions can catch out horses that need a fast surface to show their best acceleration, rewarding any runner that handles the give underfoot with a smooth, energy-efficient cruising style turning in.

watchPoints.text: No natural front-runner exists in this field — watch the first two furlongs closely, as the pace is likely to be dangerously slow, compressing the field and setting up a high-risk sprint finish that could produce significant interference.

Sarangpur and Sonnerie Power both carry STYLE_FIT flags under 0.93, meaning they are genuine hold-up horses mapped closer to midfield by necessity — if neither settles comfortably, they may be shuffled back and lose ground at a critical point.

Maywedance has the most directly relevant course-and-distance form (won 12f Kempton Standard recently) and should be monitored for market support in the final minutes before the off as a potential market mover.

Valentine Boy's step up in trip from 8f to 1m3f is untested — watch to see whether Jude Fernandes rides conservatively to settle the horse early, or whether the hood encourages a more forward pitch that could change the race shape unexpectedly.

Standard to Slow conditions across all races on the card suggest the surface is playing consistently slower than standard — horses with any concern about soft-ish AW surfaces should be noted, particularly Distinction whose best form has come in different conditions.

races.name: Unibet/British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Unibet/EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Alshera
runners_data.note: Won sole career start over 1m2f on Standard AW and steps up to 1m3f here for Gosden; the sole confirmed front-runner, she sets the pace entirely on her own terms, but 246 days off means fitness is the one question against an otherwise commanding tactical position.

runners_data.name: Crack Of Thunder
runners_data.note: Consistent non-winner whose Proform record shows a tendency to fade late; a genuine hold-up horse whose true style cannot be accommodated here — forced to race closer than natural, which dilutes the finishing kick that is her only weapon, and her 0/16 trainer 14-day record adds no confidence.

runners_data.name: Skittish
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for Hughie Morrison returning after a long absence (205 days since a jockey report entry), with stamina form over marathon trips on soft ground; the 1m3f AW trip on a quicker surface is a significant unknown, and she will need the pace to be genuinely searching to deliver her finish.

runners_data.name: Stopherandgo
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old hold-up mare who has raced exclusively at extreme distances (19f–25f) on Good to Soft ground; the drop to 1m3f on AW is a radical departure from her profile and she is a major unknown quantity in this context.

runners_data.name: Tide Lines
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for Charlie Johnston returning after 77 days, with her only recent run a fourth over 1m on Good — she steps up in trip here and needs the tempo to be compressed enough to deliver a late challenge, which is structurally difficult given Alshera's controlled front-running.

runners_data.name: Baba Ganoush
runners_data.note: Unraced or debut filly for Hughie Morrison with no public form and unknown style; David Probert is a capable claimer of opportunities but there is simply no evidence on which to base a positional or form assessment, making her a pure unknown.

runners_data.name: Blue Hill
runners_data.note: Lightly raced filly (one run, fifth over 1m on Good) with unknown style for an unfashionable yard; stepping up considerably in trip and surface type, and the single piece of form offers little to suggest she can compete at this level against more experienced rivals.

runners_data.name: Cracking Beauty
runners_data.note: Long-absent two-year-old returning after 230 days for Roger Teal; her sole start was 11th on AW and she fades in finishes — a true hold-up type pushed into midfield by the field's composition, which further compromises a profile that was already unconvincing on form.

runners_data.name: Kashooda
runners_data.note: Placed third on her only start over 1m2f on this very surface for Andrew Balding, and Oisin Murphy takes the ride — the combination of proven AW form, course and distance experience, and a top jockey makes her the most evidentially grounded of the improvers, with an unknown but likely tracking style.

runners_data.name: Make A Splash
runners_data.note: Finished ninth over 1m2f on Good last time for Tom Ward; a hold-up type whose true style is displaced to midfield by the field's composition — the poor recent form, tendency to fade, and unfavourable tactical position all point against her.

runners_data.name: Marianita
runners_data.note: Fourth on debut over 1m2f on Good for Ralph Beckett, an operation that regularly improves horses markedly on their second start; unknown style but likely to track the pace, and the step up in trip may suit if she has trained on.

runners_data.name: Salve Allegra
runners_data.note: Seventh over 1m3f on AW last time for Alan King, wearing headgear (hood); hold-up style and a fade tendency on similar ground paint a difficult picture, though the hood can sharpen a horse's early responsiveness and she has at least proven she stays the trip.

runners_data.name: Bintwafaa
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's hold-up filly, fifth over 1m on AW last time wearing headgear (hood); a non-runner here, so noted for completeness — her true position at the rear cannot be secured in this field's composition, and the trainer's 7/23 14-day record is a minor positive for connections.

races.paceDynamic: Alshera is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner field and, with no genuine rival to press her, should stride into a comfortable lead from the outset and dictate terms at a measured, sustainable gallop on the Standard to Slow Kempton AW surface. The pace she sets is unlikely to be truly searching, meaning the race will be run to suit those who can travel in her slipstream rather than those who need a genuinely strong tempo to close from far back. Crack Of Thunder, Cracking Beauty, Make A Splash, and Bintwafaa are all true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map simply because this field carries more hold-up types than can realistically race at the rear — their true style will not be accommodated and their finishing kicks are compromised by this shape. With a single front-runner setting a controlled tempo and a cluster of nominal hold-up types forced to race closer than ideal, this race shape strongly favours prominent or early-tracking runners who can latch onto Alshera's fractions and quicken from a position of comfort — hold-up horses dependent on a fast pace to deliver their finish are at a structural disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Alshera Controls, Trackers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Alshera leads unchallenged and sets a steady, controlled gallop that suits prominent racers travelling just behind.
scenarios.body: Alshera dictates from the front at a measured pace on the slow-ish surface, and horses who track her comfortably in the first two or three are best placed to challenge in the straight; the lack of genuine pace pressure means closers are unlikely to make up meaningful ground from the rear. Kashooda, Marianita, and Tide Lines — capable of racing prominently or in mid-division tracking the leader — profile best for this scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Alshera Dictates And Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Alshera's solo lead gives her a rhythm advantage and the field behind fails to organise a coherent challenge.
scenarios.body: Unchallenged in front on a track that rewards prominent runners, Alshera converts her positional advantage into a winning one, using her class (Gosden yard) and fitness coming off a 246-day break with a racecourse win already to her name; the absence of a pressing rival means she is never forced to expend energy fighting for the lead. True hold-up horses redistributed into midfield cannot generate the sustained late momentum needed to reel her in from off a slow tempo.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Gifts Hold-Up Runner
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is genuinely slow enough to compress the field so that a hold-up horse tracks midfield and produces a decisive late burst.
scenarios.body: A slow-burn gallop can occasionally compress the field sufficiently that a horse with a strong turn of foot — even one forced to race closer than ideal — produces a winning sprint finish in the Kempton straight; Tide Lines and Skittish are hold-up types with mile-plus form who could benefit if the pace becomes processional and the straight turns into a sprint.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Improver Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unexposed fillies improves sharply on debut or previous form to outclass the field as it settles into a predictable rhythm.
scenarios.body: With several lightly raced and unknown-style three-year-olds in the field, a big step forward from Blue Hill, Baba Ganoush, or Marianita — handled by shrewd trainers — cannot be ruled out if raw ability trumps positional disadvantage; Oisin Murphy on Kashooda (Andrew Balding, placed last time at 1m2f on this surface) gives that runner the most credible case among the improvers.

watchPoints.text: Alshera is the only confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner field — if she jumps cleanly and immediately establishes her lead unchallenged, she controls the race entirely and any horse that fails to track her closely within the first two furlongs is racing against the shape.

Crack Of Thunder, Make A Splash, Cracking Beauty, and Bintwafaa are all true hold-up horses who cannot get their natural position in this field — watch in the early stages whether they are forced wide or blocked in midfield, which compounds the structural disadvantage already flagged.

The going is reported Standard to Slow, which adds time to the race but also tends to reward horses who race prominently and avoid covering extra ground — any hold-up runner forced wide on the turn will be doubly exposed.

Kashooda (Oisin Murphy, Andrew Balding) is the only runner with proven course-and-distance form on this surface, having finished third over 1m2f here — watch whether Murphy positions her to track Alshera from the outset, as that would be the optimal tactical ride for this scenario.

Marianita (Rossa Ryan, Ralph Beckett) is having only her second career start and Beckett's record of improving fillies between runs is notable — watch her price movement and early positioning as a potential improver who may be underestimated on raw form.

races.name: Unibet More Extra Place Races Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Caprelo
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Hughie Morrison with Tom Marquand, winning twice on Standard going at 16f and clearly suited by a long-distance Kempton trip, though the STYLE_FIT tag signals it is racing slightly out of its optimal role; 47 days off and a blinker noted — watch whether it can replicate its best without pressure from rivals.
runners_data.comment: Caprelo won four starts back over today's distance and going, showed up again when second two starts back, but was only fourth last time; our rating of 86 keeps him firmly in the shake-up. First-time blinkers are fitted, with 136lb and 47 days off the small concerns.

runners_data.name: Baileys Khelstar
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy partners this consistent Charlie Johnston runner who has four wins and places from his last six starts, with a recent win at Goodwood over 16f on a similar surface profile; naturally prominent and well-drawn to track Caprelo comfortably, making this an obvious fit for the predicted race shape.
runners_data.comment: Baileys Khelstar won last time out over today's distance and going, having been runner-up in three of his previous four starts; our rating of 86 makes him hard to beat on a quick reappearance. The 136lb weight is his only obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Barenboim
runners_data.note: Tom Dascombe's eight-year-old wears a hood and is a genuine hold-up type whose sim-going form shows only one win from nine efforts; recent form includes two nines and a six over 16-18f, suggesting fitness concerns, and Pierre-Louis Jamin will need an unusually strong pace to get him involved.
runners_data.comment: Barenboim won six starts back, then ran a good second, but has fallen away to a string of defeats since; our rating of 84 keeps him prominent, and first-time cheekpieces may spark a reversal. That recent dip is the obvious worry.

runners_data.name: Nunc Est Bibendum
runners_data.note: Gary & Gary Moore's five-year-old has won three of his last four over 16f on Standard going, making him one of the most convincing course-and-distance profiles in the race; prominent in style and 71 days off, but a horse with that depth of Standard-going form over this exact trip demands respect if fresh and ready.
runners_data.comment: Nunc Est Bibendum won three in a row before an off day, then returned with a good second last time over today's distance and going; our rating of 79 keeps her involved. A 71-day break and a cold yard are the concerns.

runners_data.name: Dust Cover
runners_data.note: Ross Burdon's lightly-raced four-year-old is a natural front-runner by instinct — three of his five recent runs show prominent or lead behaviour — but this field is too competitive at the front end for him to secure that position naturally, and he is mapped to midfield against the grain of how he races best.
runners_data.comment: Dust Cover strung together back-to-back wins before fading, and could only finish fifth last time out 54 days ago; our rating of 77 leaves him toward the bottom of this field. Today's going holds no fears, the one thing in his favour.

runners_data.name: Gooloogong
runners_data.note: Neil Callan takes the mount on George Baker's six-year-old who has two wins from five starts at 16f on Standard going; a prominent type who should track the leader comfortably and whose strong course form makes him a legitimate threat in Scenario A if he travels smoothly in second or third.
runners_data.comment: Gooloogong won two of his last four starts, sandwiched around a third, before a below-par fourth last time out over today's distance and going; our rating of 82 still keeps him a leading threat. That dip 42 days ago is the one query.

runners_data.name: Kitty Foyle
runners_data.note: 318 days off the track (with a 50-day Flat return noted) is the dominant headline here for Oliver Carmichael and Daisy Hitchins — all recent form is over 24-25f on Good ground at a very different distance profile, and with zero sim-going wins from 15 recorded efforts, the step back in trip on AW is a significant query.
runners_data.comment: Kitty Foyle has been a model of consistency, twice runner-up in her last four starts over today's distance and going, but is yet to win and our rating of 76 leaves her down the field at eighth of nine. Her placed form confirms she stays competitive.

runners_data.name: One Cool Dreamer
runners_data.note: Alan King's five-year-old is a natural prominent racer who has been in work 110 days — his instinct is to travel up with the pace, but the crowded front end means Luke Morris is likely to find him settled back in midfield where his zero wins from six Standard-going outings are a concern for his chance here.
runners_data.comment: One Cool Dreamer is yet to win but was a good second two starts back among mostly minor-placed efforts; our rating of 77 keeps him in this midfield mix, fitted with first-time cheekpieces. A 110-day absence is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Louie's Folly
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's Irish-trained four-year-old arrives 124 days off (57-day Flat return), ridden by claimer Gina Mangan, with a form string showing no win in five outings on comparable going; a genuine hold-up type whose best recent effort was a second over 16f on Soft, and this looks a tough spot on current evidence.
runners_data.comment: Louie's Folly is yet to win, with a best of second three starts back among modest efforts over today's distance and going; our rating of 69 puts her last of nine. A stable without a single success in the last fortnight adds to the concerns.

races.paceDynamic: Caprelo is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead on paper, should dictate from the front at a sustainable, measured gallop over this 2m Kempton AW trip on Standard to Slow going. Baileys Khelstar, Nunc Est Bibendum, and Gooloogong are all naturally prominent types who will jostle for the positions immediately behind, meaning the early order could be fractious enough to slightly inflate the pace but unlikely to dislodge Caprelo from the front. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all get their natural position — Dust Cover and One Cool Dreamer are genuine prominent racers who are likely to find themselves shuffled back into midfield against their instincts, compromising their chance. A controlled, front-end gallop set by Caprelo over two miles on an AW surface strongly favours horses who can sit handy in the first three or four and sustain their effort through the long Kempton straight, giving the edge to settled prominent types over true hold-up runners.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Caprelo Controls, Prominent Follow
scenarios.trigger: If Caprelo dictates an unchallenged, honest gallop and the race is run at a consistent tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Caprelo leads at a fair but manageable pace, with Baileys Khelstar and Nunc Est Bibendum tracking closely, and the race is effectively won from the front two furlongs out as those on the pace kick through. Horses that sat handy and sustain their gallop up the straight reap the reward of the predictable tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Emerge
scenarios.trigger: If Caprelo sets an unusually slow early gallop and the race turns into a sprint finish off a falsely slow pace.
scenarios.body: The bunched field produces a sprint over the final two furlongs, which negates the distance advantage of the front-runners and opens the door to the deeper hold-up horses making late ground. Barenboim and Kitty Foyle, who both sit off the pace naturally, could pick up stragglers if the closing kick materialises.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Hotly Contested Early
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types — particularly Gooloogong and Baileys Khelstar — press Caprelo hard through the first mile and elevate the tempo.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop than expected burns off the front-end types earlier and the race sets up for those who have been ridden more patiently in midfield to come through late. Nunc Est Bibendum, with strong Standard going form and multiple wins over this sort of trip, has the tactical versatility to benefit from a well-run race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Disrupt Shape
scenarios.trigger: If Dust Cover or One Cool Dreamer manage to work forward against expectations and create an unusually contentious pace scenario.
scenarios.body: Being forced wide or into unfavoured positions from which they must expend energy to recover disrupts the race shape for everyone, potentially gifting the race to whichever horse settles best in an unsettled field. This scenario is inherently low-probability given both horses carry a style-fit discount and are unlikely to secure their natural position.

watchPoints.text: Baileys Khelstar with Oisin Murphy sits right in the pocket of the dominant race shape — watch whether he tracks Caprelo's lead comfortably through the first mile, as any smooth positioning there signals he is the horse most likely to strike.

Dust Cover and One Cool Dreamer may attempt to push forward from their likely midfield draws — if either horse is prominent early it inflates the pace and destabilises Scenario A, which is worth monitoring at the start.

Nunc Est Bibendum is 71 days off with three recent 16f Standard wins; if he is fit and travelling smoothly by halfway his prominent style and course form make him a live danger that could easily be underrated.

Kitty Foyle's 318-day absence and very different form profile (24-25f, Good turf) means any strong market move for her at Standard to Slow over 2m on AW should be treated with caution — the fitness and surface question marks are genuine.

The Standard to Slow going description is slightly slower than the headline Standard, which marginally favours horses with stamina reserves over pure speed — this tilts the balance very slightly towards the further-distance profiles like Nunc Est Bibendum and away from the horses stepping up from shorter.

races.name: Unibet Supporting Safer Gambling Handicap

runners_data.name: Roi De Coeur
runners_data.note: Marco Ghiani rides for in-form Marco Botti; a hold-up performer who showed encouraging form over this 8f trip on Standard ground but has yet to win or place on similar going in three attempts — needs others to do the forcing.
runners_data.comment: Roi De Coeur's last three runs have brought 5th, 6th and 7th, yet he still tops our figures. Winless in that spell, he returns 23 days on from a run over today's trip, and rates the biggest danger despite the absence of a recent placing.

runners_data.name: Thestral
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer juvenile who actually won over 7f on Standard and placed again at the trip; Neil Callan's booking is a positive, and his ability to race in mid-division without cover gives him a tactical advantage over true deep closers in this congested field.
runners_data.comment: Thestral was a close 3rd last time out, having been runner-up two starts before that, and that progressive trend makes him our selection here. Proven over today's trip and ground, with a win among his last five starts, he looks sure to go close.

runners_data.name: Tales Old As Time
runners_data.note: 258 days off the track is a significant freshness concern, and a noted tendency to fade in the finish makes the Standard To Slow surface unwelcome; placed once in three similar-going starts but the layoff profile is hard to trust.
runners_data.comment: Tales Old As Time's last three starts brought unplaced, 8th and a 3rd (three back), but he steps in today after a 258-day absence. Trip and ground are both proven, so he can't be ruled out from midfield, though that lay-off is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Thisonesforyou
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner, Clive Cox-trained and given a modest OR=63; her style fit score of 0.93 signals she is racing outside her typical role but that note applies less critically here given she IS the pace-setter — Georgia Dobie simply needs to use the position naturally.
runners_data.comment: Thisonesforyou won three starts back but has since dipped, with a 5th two runs later and a 9th last time out. He returns 25 days on, with today's trip already covered, leaving him a workable midfield type rather than a standout on our figures.

runners_data.name: Music Academy
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett hold-up filly wearing a visor; she has placed in two of four Standard/similar-going starts but is coming off a 30-day break and has struggled on soft, so the AW surface should suit better than her recent form implies.
runners_data.comment: Music Academy's recent form reads 6th, 7th, 3rd and 9th, her best a 3rd three starts back, and she remains winless in that spell. Trip and ground are both proven, but she rates near the bottom of this field and looks held on the evidence so far.

runners_data.name: Katalyst
runners_data.note: William Muir & Grassick-trained; a genuine hold-up horse whose true style is well to the rear, though the volume of closers in this field means he is unlikely to find his natural pitch — blinkers fitted, zero wins or places in 10 similar-going starts is damning.
runners_data.comment: Katalyst has yet to threaten in this sequence, her form reading unplaced, 4th, 6th, 5th and 6th, with a best of 4th two starts back. First-time blinkers today offer a possible wake-up call, but she still ranks near the foot of our figures on what she's shown.

runners_data.name: Roccobear
runners_data.note: J R Jenkins runner who prefers to come from off the pace; seven runs on Standard going without a win or a place paints a clear picture, and 57 days off adds uncertainty — held up by nature but the crowded rear means he faces a positional squeeze.
runners_data.comment: Roccobear ran an eye-catching 2nd four starts back and was a solid 3rd last time out, with trip and ground both proven. He returns 57 days after that run and rates one of the biggest threats on our figures, the lay-off his main concern.

runners_data.name: Sports Day
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand takes the ride for Michael Bell; though he scored over 10f on Good, his single similar-going run produced a 10th-place finish, and his true hold-up style will be hard to deploy with so many rivals contesting the same ground at the back.
runners_data.comment: Sports Day's form has been mixed, a promising 2nd three starts back sandwiched by lesser efforts, including an unplaced run last time out. He returns 23 days on with trip and ground both proven, leaving him with modest each-way claims from midfield.

runners_data.name: Torbados
runners_data.note: Charles Hills sends out a horse who placed over 7f on Standard; blinkers fitted, 43-day break, and a natural hold-up profile that the congested midfield will frustrate — his best form is over shorter distances than today's mile.
runners_data.comment: Torbados ran a creditable 3rd four starts back, and although the finishes either side have been modest, he ranks highly on our figures for this race. He returns 43 days on with first-time blinkers fitted, and looks a leading threat, more consistency the obvious ask.

runners_data.name: Ten Cuidado
runners_data.note: Mark Usher youngster returning after 189 days off; ran exclusively over 5-7f previously, so this step up to a mile on Standard To Slow is an untested combination, and his true back-of-the-field style leaves him with most ground to make up.
runners_data.comment: Ten Cuidado's best in this sequence was a 4th three starts back, either side of which he was well beaten, and he now returns from a 189-day absence. He has raced over today's trip before, but sits bottom of our figures and looks up against it.

runners_data.name: Positive Thoughts
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy's booking for the Quinn yard is the headline — the only runner alongside Thisonesforyou with a genuine prominent profile, and his ability to sit a close second throughout is potentially more valuable than his recent form figures suggest.
runners_data.comment: Positive Thoughts was runner-up five starts back but dipped through the middle of that sequence, rallying only to 5th last time out. First-time cheekpieces today, and a proven relationship with this trip, could help, but she needs to rediscover that early form to feature strongly.

runners_data.name: Blue Celestial
runners_data.note: James Tate has had six winners in the last 23 days; Saffie Osborne on a horse with a consistent placing record (five places in nine similar-going runs), and though his hold-up style puts him in the rear-side congestion, his course and distance form makes him one to respect if any late run comes off.
runners_data.comment: Blue Celestial has been remarkably consistent without a win, with 3rd, 4th, 2nd, 3rd, 7th and 4th across her last six starts and a 2nd three back her best. A quick reappearance 10 days on, proven trip and ground, and a yard in good recent form all support her each-way claims.

runners_data.name: Betty Lemon
runners_data.note: Hughie Morrison filly only 15 days since last run; she won over 8f on Good and has a placing record on Standard, but a natural hold-up tendency means she is buried in the pack at the rear in this shape, and Rose Dawes's 5lb claim is a modest compensation.
runners_data.comment: Betty Lemon won last time out, the clear highlight of a sequence otherwise reading 4th, unplaced, 7th and 4th. Trip and ground are both proven, but she rates near the bottom of our figures here and needs to find more to trouble this field.

runners_data.name: Fallacious Promise
runners_data.note: Luke Morris rides just two days after her last run — very quick turnaround for John Butler; she has placed in four of eight Standard-going starts and won over 8f on Standard, so the surface suits, and her recent form string of 1-2-3-2 makes her the most in-form horse in the race despite being mapped away from her preferred deep-closing position.
runners_data.comment: Fallacious Promise strung together a 2nd, 2nd and 3rd before winning last time out, a clear upward trend. He returns just two days later, with trip and ground both proven, giving him solid claims, though such a rapid turnaround remains unproven.

races.paceDynamic: Thisonesforyou is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner handicap and, with no genuine rival to press her, she should be able to ease into a controlled, unchallenged lead from the gates at Kempton's Polytrack mile. Positive Thoughts is the only other mapped prominent type and, while she may track Thisonesforyou, she is unlikely to force a truly searching gallop, meaning the pace is set to be modest rather than pressured. The Standard To Slow going report compounds this — slower ground on the All-Weather typically stretches the field and makes early position even more valuable, compressing the time available for hold-up horses to deliver late. The field is overwhelmingly stacked with hold-up types, and with Katalyst, Roccobear, Sports Day, Torbados, Ten Cuidado, Blue Celestial, Betty Lemon and Fallacious Promise all genuine come-from-behind horses who cannot all settle in their natural rear position, the midfield is congested and traffic will be a factor; horses who can race prominently or at least in the first third without overexerting early hold the clearest tactical edge, and Thisonesforyou's uncontested lead in a slow-ground mile strongly favours front-running and prominent racing profiles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Thisonesforyou Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Thisonesforyou sets a controlled, uncontested pace and the Standard To Slow surface ensures the tempo never truly accelerates.
scenarios.body: She bowls along in front without a rival to pressure her, conserving enough energy to kick again entering the straight; the Standard To Slow condition blunts the finishing speed of deep closers who need a true end-to-end gallop to peg her back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate Home Straight
scenarios.trigger: If Positive Thoughts tracks Thisonesforyou closely and the pair pull clear of a congested midfield pack in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The slow ground and large field create a muddled midfield with plenty of shuffling and traffic, leaving the two prominent horses with unobstructed runs and a decisive positional advantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves deceptively quick enough in the middle stages to tie up the front two before the turn for home.
scenarios.body: A handful of well-positioned hold-up horses find clear runs and finish with purpose, but only those who have managed to work closer than their natural style permits stand to benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Falters, Midfield Surges
scenarios.trigger: If Thisonesforyou ties up badly in the closing stages having set even a marginally too-strong gallop on the slow surface.
scenarios.body: A runner that has tracked midfield and finds the clearest passage on the inside or wide sweep gets the bob in a messy finish, but the congested nature of the pack means the winner is hard to identify cleanly.

watchPoints.text: Thisonesforyou (Georgia Dobie) — watch whether she is allowed to coast in front unchallenged at the halfway point; if she is still travelling comfortably turning for home with daylight ahead, she becomes a major factor at a short price.

Fallacious Promise (Luke Morris) — back just two days after her last run with four placed efforts in her last five, she is the most consistently performing horse in the field and any sign of a clear run turning in should put punters on alert.

Positive Thoughts (Oisin Murphy) — the Murphy booking for a quietly-fancied yard elevates this horse significantly; if she tracks Thisonesforyou throughout and is still on the bridle two furlongs out, the race may not go as far forward as expected.

Blue Celestial (Saffie Osborne, James Tate T14: 6/23) — the trainer is firing at nearly 26% in the last fortnight and this consistent placer has strong course form; worth monitoring in the market for any late support.

Congestion at the rear — with eight horses all preferring to be held up and unable to secure their natural position, watch for traffic reports in the straight; any horse who finds an unobstructed wide passage from two furlongs out gains a significant mechanical advantage.

races.name: Try Unibet's New Improved Acca Boosts Handicap (Div 1)

runners_data.name: Volto Di Medusa
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with a win at 8f on Standard AW in recent form, but the sim-going record of 2 wins from 15 similar starts is modest; 22 days since last run and the slow tempo this race will be run at is a structural disadvantage for a horse that needs a genuine gallop to finish off.|
runners_data.comment: Volto Di Medusa won two starts back over today's distance and going but was unplaced last time out 22 days ago; our rating of 67 places him fourth of eleven on that mixed picture. First-time cheekpieces could yet spark an improvement.

runners_data.name: Platinum Prince
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed pace-setter who will shape the entire contest from the front; his sim-going record here is thin (2 from 15) and a 33-day absence adds risk, but his role as uncontested leader at a modest gallop is his primary asset in this field. Style fit flagged as 0.93 racing out of his role historically, though on this occasion his natural lead position is exactly what the race demands.|
runners_data.comment: Platinum Prince won five starts back, then a good second, but has dipped over his last two, including only fifth last time over today's distance and going; our rating of 74 still leaves him second-best here. First-time blinkers offer hope of a reversal.

runners_data.name: Thapa VC
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer whose recent form shows a string of placed efforts over shorter distances; Oisin Murphy taking the ride is a significant booking upgrade, and the horse's Standard AW experience (6 from 15 sim-going runs) is solid, though the steady tempo suits him less than a genuinely-run mile.|
runners_data.comment: Thapa Vc is yet to win but has been rock-solid, runner-up last time out over today's distance and going after a run of minor-placed efforts; our rating of 75 makes him the one to beat here. First-time tongue-tie and blinkers add further interest, and he races from stall eleven.

runners_data.name: Six Blue
runners_data.note: A hold-up runner whose last six starts have all been over trips longer than today's mile, and the sharp drop to 8f at Kempton on a slow tempo does not play to his strengths; three from six on similar going but the distance reduction is a question mark.|
runners_data.comment: Six Blue is yet to win, with modest figures of fifth, fifth and sixth in her limited outings, though she does have today's going form and our rating of 68 still places her third of eleven. A 58-day absence is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Gladiadora
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer with two wins in five starts on Standard AW and excellent course-distance profile at Kempton; Saffie Osborne aboard a horse showing fresh handicap form 18 days ago, and the moderate gallop set by Platinum Prince is exactly the scenario where she can track and kick. One of the best-placed horses for this precise race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Gladiadora won five starts back, runner-up soon after, but has since faded to a mix of fourths and an eighth, the latest just 18 days ago; our rating of 64 leaves her mid-pack at sixth of eleven, with today's distance previously covered.

runners_data.name: Relevant Range
runners_data.note: Elle-May Croot (5lb claim) partners this prominent-style handicapper who has a strong sim-going record of 2 wins from 9 Standard AW starts over 8f; 16 days since last run and the field may be deeper than she has recently handled, but she is correctly placed tactically for this shape.|
runners_data.comment: Relevant Range is yet to win but rallied for a promising second last time out over today's distance 16 days ago; our rating of 64 keeps him in this midfield mix. A yard with just one success from 32 runners in the last fortnight is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Mbappe
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse by profile but mapped to midfield because the field is over-supplied with closers; one win on Standard AW at this distance is a positive, but the 0.92 style-fit flag reflects the reality that he is unlikely to get the late-run opportunity his best form requires. His chance here is contingent on conditions that this race shape will not generate.|
runners_data.comment: Mbappe won three starts back, but has slipped since to sixth and seventh, the latter just 13 days ago over today's distance and going; our rating of 62 keeps him only seventh of eleven. First-time cheekpieces are the intended spark.

runners_data.name: Chico Dulce
runners_data.note: Course specialist with multiple starts at 8f on Standard AW (13 from 15 sim-going runs), including a win at this track and distance; 79 days off is the main concern for trainer Madgwick, but the prominent style and intimate knowledge of Kempton's demands make him a serious contender if the layoff has been well-managed.|
runners_data.comment: Chico Dulce won four starts back over today's distance and going, but has since faded to a fifth, fourth and seventh; our rating of 60 keeps him mid-table at eighth of eleven. That lengthy 79-day absence is the obvious question.

runners_data.name: Luminous Approach
runners_data.note: Four-year-old whose short form string (4 runs visible) shows no win on Standard AW; bumped to midfield from a natural hold-up position, meaning David Probert will need to manufacture a closer's run in a race that will not be strongly run. The 0.90 style-fit flag and 60-day absence combine to make this a difficult assignment.|
runners_data.comment: Luminous Approach is yet to win, with modest figures of unplaced, sixth, seventh and fifth across his last four starts over today's distance and going; our rating of 58 leaves him ninth of eleven. A 60-day absence adds to the concerns.

runners_data.name: Lovely Jubly
runners_data.note: A fading-finish flag accompanies this hold-up mare who has been off for 210 days — the longest layoff in the field by a significant margin; even in her best form she struggled for a telling finish, and being displaced from her preferred rear position into midfield makes a winning performance hard to construct here.|
runners_data.comment: Lovely Jubly won three starts back over today's distance and going but has been below that level since, sixth and eighth in her last two; our rating of 53 leaves her tenth of eleven after a lengthy 210-day absence.

runners_data.name: Summer Evening
runners_data.note: Young hold-up filly who is pushed into midfield from her natural position at the rear, having shown no wins in 14 starts on similar going; Tyler Heard rides but the combination of lowest OR in the field (46), an unplaced recent run at 8f on soft ground, and a structural disadvantage in this pace shape makes this a very tough task.|
runners_data.comment: Summer Evening is yet to win, with modest recent figures capped by a well-beaten ninth last time out over today's distance, 20 days ago; our rating of 49 leaves her bottom of this field of eleven. Little from the facts inspires confidence here.

races.paceDynamic: Platinum Prince is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner field and, with no genuine rival prepared to press him hard from the outset, he is set to control proceedings at a measured, self-regulated tempo over Kempton's flat mile. The going is Standard to Slow on the AW surface, which will add a fraction of extra effort to each stride and makes a truly searching gallop from the front even less likely — Platinum Prince can coast along at a pace that suits him perfectly. Gladiadora and Relevant Range are the most likely to track him in the prominent positions, with Chico Dulce also capable of sitting just off the early tempo. This shape — a single, unhurried pace-setter dictating a steady to moderate gallop — strongly favours horses that can race on or just off the pace in the first three or four, as the lack of genuine pressure means the winner is unlikely to be produced from the rear of the field; late runners will face a steadily-run race that does not generate enough tempo to bring them into play off a true staying test. The field contains markedly more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the back — Mbappe, Luminous Approach, Lovely Jubly, and Summer Evening are all genuine closers who are likely to be pushed forward out of their natural position or find themselves racing in conditions that will not suit their style.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Platinum Prince Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Platinum Prince is allowed to control the pace from the front without any rival applying pressure, creating a steady gallop that suits those racing prominently.
scenarios.body: Platinum Prince sets a comfortable tempo, with Gladiadora and Relevant Range tucked in behind and able to use their tactical position to strike from two furlongs out; the lack of a genuine pace injection from the rear means hold-up runners have no accelerating tempo to chase. Prominent racers who can quicken off a modest gallop are the chief beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Modest Pace, Front Pair Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Platinum Prince and Gladiadora form a lead pair and the gallop is genuinely slow, allowing only the first two or three to sprint clear at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A slowly-run affair sees the principals effectively race in a small group at the head of affairs, and those with the tactical awareness to sit just behind the leader have first run on the field; Chico Dulce, whose form is heavily weighted to this course and distance at Standard going, is well placed to pounce. Hold-up horses remain stranded as the winner is decided inside the final two furlongs by those already in contention.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Outrun Moderate Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally stronger than anticipated — perhaps forced by Relevant Range or Gladiadora pushing forward — creating enough of a gallop for a hold-up horse to close.
scenarios.body: Thapa VC or Mbappe, if able to secure a decent position closer to the pace than their nominal map position suggests, could use a genuinely-run mile to close into the contest in the final furlong; however, the redistribution flags on Mbappe and others mean their chances of being truly held-up and then finishing with a meaningful run are markedly reduced. This scenario is structurally less likely because the horses who would exploit it are not natural closers in this race shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Capitalises Fully
scenarios.trigger: If Platinum Prince, racing in his preferred role, converts the uncontested lead directly into victory by simply never relinquishing it to the prominent trackers.
scenarios.body: With no pace pressure applied, Platinum Prince quickens from the front in the final quarter-mile before Gladiadora or Relevant Range can organise their challenge; the Standard to Slow surface rewards a horse conserving energy throughout rather than sprinting late. This is a low-probability standalone outcome given his limited similar-going record and the presence of well-handicapped rivals in behind.

watchPoints.text: Gladiadora is the horse to watch most closely — if she tracks Platinum Prince in second or third and Saffie Osborne times the challenge from two furlongs out, the steady pace will have left her entirely fresh and she is best placed of any runner to exploit this shape.

Platinum Prince's ability to control the tempo without being pressured is the fulcrum of the entire race; if anything — Relevant Range or an unexpected move by Chico Dulce — pushes him into a faster first half, the dynamic shifts toward hold-up runners and his chance evaporates.

Chico Dulce's 79-day absence is the key unknown for Michael Madgwick's yard; if he shows any sign of ring-rustiness in the opening furlong and fails to slot in prominently, his strong course form becomes irrelevant because there will be nothing to chase him into the race late.

Mbappe, Luminous Approach, Lovely Jubly, and Summer Evening are all genuine closers forced into midfield by the overcrowded hold-up section — monitor the draw and early positioning at the start; if more than two of them attempt to race further forward than expected, the pace map changes materially.

The going is confirmed Standard to Slow for the 8:20 race — any further deterioration in conditions during the evening would incrementally favour horses with front-running or prominent styles who expend less energy chasing a pace that never truly materialises.

races.name: Try Unibet's New Improved Acca Boosts Handicap (Div 2)

runners_data.name: Spirit Lead Me
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Richard Hughes with course experience at this trip, but the ⚠ fades-in-finish flag is a material concern in a race that will almost certainly end in a sprint; Donagh Murphy's 7lb claim helps compensate on weight, and the sim-going record of 8 from 15 suggests the surface is familiar if not dominant.
runners_data.comment: Spirit Lead Me has been well held throughout, his best a 6th six starts back, with 8th, 9th, 9th and 9th following before a similar 8th last time out. First-time cheekpieces and proven form over trip and ground offer some hope, but he still has plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Union Island
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston stable in solid 14-day form (5/48) and this five-year-old boasts a win over 8f at Goodwood earlier in the season; Jack Callan (3lb claimer) keeps the weight low and the horse's Goodwood mile form translates well to a flat, galloping AW layout — one of the more credible finishers here.
runners_data.comment: Union Island won five starts back and has stayed competitive since, with 5th, 4th, 3rd and 4th in between, putting him firmly in this midfield mix. First-time cheekpieces and proven trip and ground form add interest, though he needs the breaks to go his way.

runners_data.name: Look Back Smiling
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride for Neil Mulholland, which commands attention, but the sim-going record of just 2 from 15 on comparable surfaces is a red flag; returning from 33 days off and with no AW win in recent form, this six-year-old needs things to fall right to make an impact.
runners_data.comment: Look Back Smiling stands out on our figures, well clear of this field despite a modest recent sequence of 4th, unplaced, 9th, 6th and unplaced. First-time cheekpieces and a 33-day break give him a fair chance to bounce back, with only that recent form the obvious query.

runners_data.name: Opening Bat
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton runner with back-to-back 11th-place finishes at Goodwood before that, though earlier form includes a third and placed efforts on Standard; true running style is hold-up but has been placed into midfield on the map as the field cannot accommodate all closers at the rear — a positional lottery awaits.
runners_data.comment: Opening Bat was a solid 3rd twice in his last five starts, form that puts him among the leading contenders here, even though his last two efforts were well beaten. With trip and ground both proven, he rates one of the main dangers if he rediscovers that level.

runners_data.name: Finn Ironside
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's five-year-old has pace figures good enough for this grade (three placed efforts over 7f at Goodwood) and hg:t (tongue-tie) suggests connections are trying to get more out of him; genuinely a hold-up horse by nature, and with eight runners from 15 on similar going he handles the surface — drawn into midfield on the map by sheer weight of closers in this field.
runners_data.comment: Finn Ironside ran a solid 3rd three starts back but has since dipped, with 8th and 7th his last two efforts. First-time tongue-tie and proven trip and ground form add interest, but a yard out of current form is a concern.

runners_data.name: Between Me And U
runners_data.note: Michael Herrington's yard has been active (4/18 in 14 days) and this horse has placed at 8f on soft and Standard, showing the trip and surface combination suits; a natural closer, slotted to midfield by the map due to field composition, the hg:t headgear change is worth noting if it sharpens focus in a bunched finish.
runners_data.comment: Between Me And U was a good 2nd four starts back but has since dipped, with 6th, 6th and 7th his last three efforts. First-time tongue-tie and proven trip and ground form add further appeal, though that recent dip is a concern.

runners_data.name: Devious Devan
runners_data.note: The most interesting form line here is a winning run at 8f Standard earlier in the season for Muir & Grassick, with the trainer duo going winless in the last 14 days (0/16); another genuine hold-up horse absorbed into midfield on the map, and the 34 days since last run may mean he needs this to find full sharpness.
runners_data.comment: Devious Devan won two starts back after a modest 7th, 8th and unplaced before that, but he came back down to earth with a 7th last time out. With trip and ground both covered, he retains each-way claims from this midfield group, on the strength of that win alone.

runners_data.name: Sub Thirteen
runners_data.note: Jeremy Scott sends this five-year-old whose recent form includes a second over 6f on Good and a third over 8f at Goodwood — the step back up to 8f may suit; classified as a natural hold-up type redistributed to midfield here, and the 0/2 trainer 14-day record suggests the yard is not firing, though Georgia Dobie's claim helps.
runners_data.comment: Sub Thirteen was a promising 2nd four starts back but form dipped after, with unplaced and 8th efforts following before a modest 3rd last time out. First-time cheekpieces add some interest, but he rates towards the foot of our figures here.

runners_data.name: Beau Jardine
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old who won last time out over 7f on Soft for Rachel Cook & John Bridger, showing he retains ability; the switch to AW and slight trip extension over 1m are the questions, and while he is a natural hold-up runner like most in this race, his recent winning form makes him one to respect if he gets a clean run in a sprint finish.
runners_data.comment: Beau Jardine won last time out having built steadily through 7th, 7th, 6th and 4th before that, a clear upward trend. First-time cheekpieces and proven trip and ground form back up that improvement, giving him solid claims from this midfield group.

runners_data.name: Hawaiian King
runners_data.note: A four-year-old for Michael Madgwick (0/1 in 14 days) who has been running at 10f and 12f and now drops markedly in trip to 8f — the distance shortening is the key uncertainty; sim-going record of 8 from 11 on comparable surfaces is fine, but the form string of 486076 offers little encouragement in a competitive handicap.
runners_data.comment: Hawaiian King's best in this spell was a fourth six starts back, and he has struggled since, no better than sixth last time. Trip and ground are both covered, but he rates second-bottom of this field.

runners_data.name: Cherry Hill
runners_data.note: The worst recent form in the field — a string of zeros and double-figures for Dominic Ffrench Davis with a sim-going record of 10 from 15 suggesting the surface does not play to her strengths; 36 days between runs, no wins in the last five, and a low OR of 45 make it hard to construct a winning scenario even in a lottery finish.
runners_data.comment: Cherry Hill has managed only a best of 8th in this sequence, with four unplaced efforts either side, and she sits bottom of our figures for this race. Trip and ground are both proven, but on this evidence she looks up against more seasoned rivals.

races.paceDynamic: This 1m Kempton AW contest on a Standard to Slow surface is a field composed almost entirely of hold-up horses with no confirmed front-runner in the lineup, meaning the early gallop is likely to be pedestrian and the race will compress into a bunched, sprint-style finish from the home turn. Without a genuine pace-setter to string the field out, the tempo will be self-regulated and slow, favouring those with a sharp finishing kick over those who need a true test of stamina. The Standard to Slow going report for this race further dulls pace, adding weight to a scenario where the field crawls early and accelerates only in the final two furlongs. Closers and hold-up horses who possess an explosive short finish will theoretically benefit, but given every runner in this field is a natural hold-up type, the race shape is volatile — positional luck, draw, and the ability to find clear running early in the straight are decisive. No runners are tagged as front-runners here; the field note confirms more prominent types than the map can place, with Opening Bat, Finn Ironside, and Between Me And U — all natural hold-up horses — redistributed to midfield, so none of them can be relied upon to inject early pace or dominate the race from the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If no horse asserts early and the field crawls to the home turn, triggering a mass sprint over the final 2f
scenarios.body: The compressed tempo means the race becomes a cavalry charge turning in, with the winner decided by positioning, draw, and a sharp burst of acceleration rather than stamina; horses with course form and a proven ability to quicken on AW surfaces thrive here

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Handy Mover Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one horse edges forward unchallenged from the outset and controls a steady tempo from a prominent position
scenarios.body: A horse that slots into a lead-adjacent role without being pressured essentially gets a solo time-trial over the final half-mile, with rivals unable to close from too far back; the horse in front entering the final furlong on this flat track rarely gets caught when the pace is honest but not burning

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If a horse is produced widest of all in the straight and benefits from a clear passage while rivals impede each other in a bunched finish
scenarios.body: In a field of hold-up runners, traffic problems are near-certain for those drawn wide or buried deep, but one horse with a clean run along the outside can pick off tiring rivals who peaked too early; the going being slower than standard slightly rewards the stayer who gets the run

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If the field fragments into pockets with several horses going nowhere at the back, leaving the race wide open for a single well-positioned runner to steal
scenarios.body: A chaotic race with no leader and eleven hold-up horses can produce a winner from an unexpected quarter if one runner flukes a passage others do not; form and class count for less in this shape, and lower-rated horses with improving profile or fresh legs may outrun their odds

watchPoints.text: Spirit Lead Me is flagged as prone to fading in the finish — in a race that will almost certainly end in a furlong-long sprint, monitor whether Donagh Murphy can time the run to avoid that late weakness repeating.

With eleven hold-up horses and no confirmed pace-setter, the opening quarter-mile could be almost walk-pace — watch for one horse (likely Between Me And U or Finn Ironside) to drift forward opportunistically and steal a march if rivals are slow to react.

Union Island has a recent win at this trip on Goodwood's flat track and Jack Callan's 3lb claim keeps weight manageable — if this horse gets a clean early position tracking the leader, it becomes a major player in the sprint finish.

Beau Jardine won last time out and is unexposed at this trip on AW — watch the market move as a guide to whether connections believe the surface and distance combination suits a horse who has mainly raced on turf recently.

The Standard to Slow going report for all seven Kempton races tonight confirms the surface is consistently slower than advertised Standard — any horse with demonstrated form on dead or slow AW going holds a measurable edge over those whose best efforts came on faster surfaces.
